decision: The implemented boundary validates unknown HTTP JSON as a RemoteResource DTO before RemoteIncidentRepository converts it into an Incident domain object. CampusOpsApiClient classifies invalid JSON as ContractError, non-2xx replies as HttpStatusError carrying only status and safe code, and aborted requests as TransportTimeoutError. RemoteIncidentRepository validates each list/detail/create DTO and rejects null or incomplete payloads before constructing domain data.
alternatives: Accept HTTP JSON as a domain Incident directly and let UI/application code discover missing or invalid fields later.
Validate the DTO at the infrastructure boundary, then convert only the flow-required validated payload to the domain Incident.
Treat all fetch, parsing and HTTP failures as one generic Error without preserving error category or safe status information.
tradeoff: Boundary validation adds DTO-to-domain mapping and explicit error types, so each new endpoint needs validation code. In return, malformed or nullable transport data cannot become invented domain state, HTTP recovery can use a status/code without logging raw server bodies, and a timeout remains distinguishable from a 500. The current repository does not persist remote responses, so failure paths cannot partially persist an incident through this adapter.
